name: Canastone
description: Canastone (meaning 'Large Canasta') is a three-deck version of Canasta played in Italy, also known as Italian Canasta. Uses 162 cards (three 52-card packs + 6 jokers). Features unique drawing rules (draw 2 from stock OR take discard pile + 1 from stock), variable discard pile size, and special bonuses for wild card and Ace canastas.

history.origins: Canastone is an Italian variant of Canasta that uses three decks instead of two. The name means 'Large Canasta' referring to the larger deck and the potential for more cards in play. It represents the Italian adaptation of the South American game.
timeline: 1940s-50s: Canasta spreads worldwide including to Italy
Mid-late 20th century: Canastone develops as Italian three-deck variant
Current: Popular in Italy, sometimes played with special red/black disc cards instead of standard suits
history.cultural: Canastone is primarily played in Italy. The game sometimes uses special cards showing red discs (instead of hearts/diamonds) and black discs (instead of spades/clubs) since only the colors matter, not the specific suits.
history.evolution: Canastone modifies classic Canasta with three decks, different drawing rules (2 from stock OR discard pile + 1), variable initial discard pile size based on the turned-up card, and special canasta types including wild card canastas and Ace canastas.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (partners opposite); can be played with 6 (two teams of 3)
setup.deck: 162 cards: three standard 52-card packs plus six jokers. Only colors (red/black) matter, not specific suits. Wild cards: jokers (mattoni) and 2s (pinelle). Natural cards: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. Threes have special functions.
setup.dealing: Partnerships by drawing cards (highest vs lowest). Dealer gives 15 cards each. Next card turned up starts discard pile (pozzo). If 3 or wild, keep turning until natural found. If first 3 all wild/3s, redeal. Dealer adds face-down packet to discard pile: size = rank of face-up card (Ace=14, King=13, ..., Four=4). If face-up 2 or joker, pile is frozen (turned sideways). Stock pile (tallone) is remaining cards.
setup.equipment: 162-card deck (or special Canastone cards with red/black discs), score sheet

rules.objective: Score points by forming melds and canastas. Special bonuses for wild card canastas and Ace canastas. Be first team to complete required canastas and go out.
rules.gameplay: Red 3s: placed face up before play, replaced with new cards. Opening (team's first meld): Can only be done at START of turn before drawing. Requirements: 50+ pts if team score <3000; 90+ pts if 3000-5000; 120+ pts if >5000. Opening player continues with normal turn. Before opening: draw 2 from stock, meld any red 3s drawn (replaced), discard 1 to end turn. After opening: draw either (a) 2 from stock, OR (b) entire discard pile + 1 from stock. Then may meld, then discard. Melds: 3+ cards same rank. Natural melds: max 2 wild cards (must have more naturals than wilds). Canasta: 7+ card meld. Clean (pulito): no wilds. Dirty (sporco): has wilds. Wild card meld: commits team to complete 7+ wild canasta; cannot use wilds elsewhere until completed. Special canastas: Wild canasta clean = all 2s or all 6 jokers+1 two; dirty = 1-5 jokers+2s. Ace canasta: 7+ aces. Threes: red 3s score separately; black 3s can only be discarded, never melded. Frozen pile: if has wild or black 3 on top, can only take if have 2 natural cards of same rank as top card in hand.
keyRules: 4 players in partnerships (or 6 in two teams of 3)
Discard pile starts with variable face-down cards (4-14 based on turned card)
Opening meld only at start of turn
Draw: 2 from stock OR discard pile + 1 from stock
Wild card meld commits team to complete it
Red 3s placed before play; black 3s only discards
Frozen pile requires 2 naturals to take

strategy.basic: Focus on making your opening meld as soon as possible. Decide whether to draw 2 from stock or take the discard pile based on what you need. Start canastas early so you can go out later.
strategy.intermediate: Coordinate with partner on which canastas to pursue. The wild card canasta is valuable (2000 pts clean) but commits you - only start if you have many wilds. Track red 3s - having 4 is great (1000 pts), but 5 is bad (-600 penalty). Manage the discard pile - taking it gives many cards but may include unwanted points.
strategy.advanced: Complex decisions about when to take the large initial discard pile. Timing your go-out to maximize bonuses or minimize opponent opportunities. Strategic freezing of the discard pile. Optimal allocation of wild cards between natural melds vs wild canasta attempt.
tips: Taking the initial discard pile can give 15+ cards - evaluate carefully
Wild canasta clean (all 2s or 6 jokers+1 two) = 2000 points
Avoid having exactly 5 red 3s (-600 penalty) or 6 (-1000)
Black 3s are safe discards that freeze the pile
Opening meld requirements increase as your score increases
Coordinate with partner - don't both work on same rank
Ace canasta (1000 pts) is easier than wild canasta
